name: Keytomic
author: Keytomic

sections.description:
Keytomic is an AI SEO platform. It researches keywords, plans a content calendar, and writes SEO articles for your website. This plugin connects your WordPress site to Keytomic, so each article goes to your site without copy and paste.

You decide in Keytomic if an article goes to WordPress as a draft for review, or as a live post. Keytomic can also refresh your older posts, and the refreshed post keeps its URL.

What the plugin does on your site

  • Publishes articles as drafts or live posts. Each article keeps its title, slug, excerpt, headings, lists, tables, images and links.
  • Sets the featured image. The plugin downloads the hero image from Keytomic one time, and does not download the same image again.
  • Adds a meta description. The plugin adds the description that Keytomic writes for each post.
  • Adds structured data. The plugin adds Keytomic’s JSON-LD (Article, FAQ and more) to each post, with the final WordPress URL of the post.
  • Updates posts safely. An update changes the same post, so the post keeps its URL, publish date and author. Keytomic never makes a duplicate post when it updates a post.
  • Works with your SEO plugin. On a post that Keytomic imported from your site, the plugin saves the description in Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress or The SEO Framework, and that plugin keeps its tags on the page.

What the plugin does not do

  • It does not write content inside WordPress. Keytomic writes the articles.
  • It does not send your site’s content anywhere. It only answers requests that Keytomic sends to your site.
  • It does not change your theme, your menus or your other posts.

What you need

  • A Keytomic account. You can start a free trial or see the plans.
  • WordPress 6.0 or later, and PHP 8.1 or later.
  • The WordPress REST API must be on. It is on by default.

External services

This plugin is designed to be used with the Keytomic platform and requires an API key generated in your Keytomic account.

This plugin does not send your site’s content to Keytomic on its own. It only processes inbound requests made to your site’s endpoint.

Data handled:
– API key (entered by the site admin and stored as a hash in WordPress options)
– Post data received from Keytomic (title, slug, summary/excerpt, content, optional hero image URL and alt text, optional SEO description, optional JSON-LD structured data)

When data is processed:
– When Keytomic sends a request to your site’s REST endpoint
– When the plugin downloads a featured image from a URL provided in the request (if used)

External service links:
– Keytomic: https://keytomic.com
– Privacy Policy: https://keytomic.com/privacy-policy
– Terms of Service: https://keytomic.com/term-and-conditions
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New, search for “Keytomic”, then click Install Now and Activate.
  2. In Keytomic, open Integrations → WordPress. Enter your site URL and click Generate key. Copy the key.
  3. In WordPress, go to Settings → Keytomic. Paste the key and click Save Changes.
  4. In Keytomic, click Test connection.

Keytomic shows the key one time. If you lose it, generate a new key in Keytomic and paste it again.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Keytomic account?

Yes. The plugin only receives the articles that Keytomic sends. Keytomic writes and plans them.

Does it publish automatically?

Only when you tell Keytomic to. You choose in Keytomic if an article goes to WordPress as a draft or as a live post.

Will it change my existing posts?

Only a post that Keytomic publishes or refreshes. An update keeps the URL, publish date and author of the post.

Does it work with Yoast SEO or Rank Math?

Yes. Keytomic posts get their own meta description and structured data. On a post that Keytomic imported from your site, your SEO plugin keeps its tags, and Keytomic saves the description in that plugin.

Does it create duplicate posts?

No. Keytomic updates the existing post. When Keytomic knows the post ID, it updates that post. Otherwise it finds the post by its slug.

Does it slow down my site?

No. The plugin runs only when Keytomic sends a request, and when a single post adds its meta description and structured data to the page head.

Is the API key stored in plain text?

No. The API key is stored as a hash and verified server-side.

Where is the endpoint?

POST /wp-json/keytomic/v1/drafts. Requests must send the header Authorization: Keytomic YOUR_API_KEY. The modes are ping (connection test), lookup, draft and publish. The content can be contentHtml, contentMarkdown or sections.
sections.changelog:
0.1.6

  • Update an existing post by its id, keep its URL and status, and refuse if that post does not exist.
  • Lookup also returns the post status, URL, modified date and page builder.
  • An update no longer clears the excerpt or meta description when the request has none, and refuses an empty body.
  • Keep backslashes in post content.
  • Imported posts keep the tags that an SEO plugin writes (Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, The SEO Framework), and a description from Keytomic is saved in that plugin.

0.1.5

  • Add a read-only lookup mode so Keytomic can confirm an existing post before it refreshes it.

0.1.4

  • Add JSON-LD structured data storage and output for Keytomic-published posts.
  • Add schema-only metadata updates so Keytomic can generate structured data from the final WordPress permalink.

0.1.3

  • Add slug-based upsert for draft/publish requests (same slug updates the same post).
  • Promote draft-to-publish on the same post when slug matches.
  • Skip duplicate hero image sideloading when the source URL is unchanged.
  • Add response metadata for create/update operations.

0.1.2

  • Internal improvements and compatibility updates.

0.1.0

  • Initial release.
  • Settings screen for API key.
  • REST endpoint for ping, draft, and publish modes.
  • Optional featured image sideloading.
  • Meta description support.
